title: Office Application Startup: Outlook Forms
summary: Outlook forms are the message templates that define the layout and the behaviour of items in a mailbox, and they are stored inside the mailbox itself rather than as loose files on disk. Because a form can carry a script behind its fields, an attacker who can write a form into a mailbox gains code that runs inside the Outlook process whenever that form is used. In the abuse pattern, the attacker first sends an email that installs a custom form into the recipient mailbox, then later sends a second message that is crafted to be rendered with that form; the script behind the form fires as the message is opened or previewed. Nothing needs to survive on the endpoint as an executable, so the technique follows the mailbox across roaming profiles and new machines, and it can reappear after the user is moved to a freshly built laptop. The artefact is a non-standard form definition stored in the mailbox and a script routine executing with Outlook as its parent process, which is why detection work sits in mailbox auditing, form inventory and the script controls that administrators apply to Outlook. Legitimate organisations do publish custom forms for travel requests or help desk tickets, so the discriminator is not the existence of a form but its origin, its age, and whether its script attempts to reach the network or start other programs.

beginner.definition: An Outlook form is a ready made template that decides how a mail message looks and behaves. This technique is when an attacker puts a harmful template into your mailbox. The template then runs hidden code inside Outlook when a special message arrives.
beginner.whyItMatters: The code is kept in your mailbox, not as a file on your computer, so it can follow you to a new machine. Antivirus tools that look at files may never see it. It is quiet and repeats every time the right message is opened, so the attacker can come back later.
howItWorks: Outlook keeps forms inside the mailbox itself, and each one can hold a small script.
The attacker sends you a message that installs one of their own forms into your mailbox.
The new form waits there quietly and loads again every time Outlook starts.
Later the attacker sends a second message built to use that form.
When you open or preview that message, the hidden script runs inside Outlook.
The script may contact the attacker or start other programs on your computer.
beginner.example: Picture a post office where customers can leave their own rubber stamp at the counter. A stranger leaves a stamp that looks ordinary. Weeks later he posts a letter and the clerk, following the stamp, quietly adds a copy of the letter to a box outside. The clerk did nothing wrong, because the stamp was on file.
takeaways: The harmful code lives in the mailbox, so it survives a rebuild of the computer.
It triggers on a later email, not at the moment the form was installed.
Review the list of custom forms in mailboxes and treat unexpected ones as suspicious.

objectives: Explain what an Outlook form is and why a form can carry executable script.
Describe how a custom form reaches a mailbox and survives an Outlook restart.
Describe how this sub-technique differs from the parent technique Office Application Startup.
Identify which mailbox and client artefacts reveal an unexpected custom form.
Explain why file based antivirus scanning may miss this persistence method.
